procedure_text: WO 99/06339 discloses a process for preparing substituted benzyl bromides by brominating the corresponding methyl aromatics in the presence of azocarboxylic esters or azonitriles and in the presence of an oxidizing agent. In this case, one substituent is electronegative and is from the group fluorine, chlorine, bromine, alkoxycarbonyl, cyano and nitro. Disadvantages of this process are the use of an additional oxidizing agent and the not always satisfactory yields.
procedure_summary: A cited earlier international application discloses the side chain bromination of methyl aromatics carrying an electronegative substituent, run in the presence of azocarboxylic esters or azonitriles together with an oxidizing agent, to give substituted benzyl bromides. The patent objects to the extra oxidant and to yields it calls not always satisfactory.
notes: This is PRIOR ART. Paragraph [0002] is the Background of the patent and every transformation in it is somebody else's disclosure, not the route this patent claims. A2 rule 5e's attribution question therefore has a plain answer here and route_attribution_unclear is not raised: nothing is unclear, and PROMPT-CORRECTIONS section 3 forbids that flag anywhere in this patent because there is no drawn scheme to attribute. The disclosure recorded here is WO 99/06339's, and the patent names two disadvantages of it in the same breath, the additional oxidizing agent and the not always satisfactory yields, which is why it cannot be read as the invention's own. It is a separate disclosure from the EP-A 0 292 944 route in Steps 2 and 3 and no material flows between them, so precursor_step is null and the linkage tag is standalone. REAGENTS: azocarboxylic esters and azonitriles are ALTERNATIVES in the text ('in the presence of azocarboxylic esters or azonitriles'), not a pair used together; both are carried as reagent, and per PROMPT-CORRECTIONS section 8 an initiator class takes reagent rather than catalyst because initiating consumes it. The brominating agent itself is never named: the text says only 'by brominating', so no bromine source is on this record and none has been supplied. mechanism_type is radical on the chemistry of an azo initiator with a benzylic side chain bromination, not on any word in the text; named_reaction is left null rather than stretched to Wohl-Ziegler, which would need N-bromosuccinimide and the text names no brominating agent at all. The scope sentence ('one substituent is electronegative and is from the group fluorine, chlorine, bromine, alkoxycarbonyl, cyano and nitro') is substituent scope on the same process and is kept inside this record's procedure_text rather than split off. cross_reference_unresolved is false: the WO number is an attribution of the disclosure, not a pointer to material or conditions stated elsewhere that could not be found. The paragraph states no charge, no temperature, no time, no pressure, no atmosphere, no workup, no purification and no yield, so scale is not_specified and no_conditions is raised. That is what the document says, not a gap in the reading, and no condition has been supplied from outside it. mass_balance_implausible is not raised because there is no mass to balance. So no structure reached this record and none of the drawing flags can apply. Per PROMPT-CORRECTIONS section 6 every compounds[] quantity here is null rather than an object of nulls. workup_type, purification and catalyst_class are skipped rather than tagged none: the paragraph describes no workup, no purification and no catalyst, and absence of a description is not a description of absence (A2 rule 26, skip rather than guess). STEP COUNT: three records, agreeing with A0's estimate of 3. The one judgement call is the Houben-Weyl sentence, 'Bromomethyl aromatics may in principle be prepared from the corresponding methyl aromatics by side chain bromination; on this subject, cf. Houben-Weyl, Vol. 5, page 331 ff. (1960)'. It is recorded here as a TEXTBOOK CITATION and not as a fourth transformation, which is A0's ruling too. The reasons: it discloses no process, only that one 'may in principle' be done, and it points at a handbook chapter with 'cf.' rather than attributing a process to a prior-art document, which is exactly what the two sentences that do get records do ('WO 99/06339 discloses a process' and 'EP-A 0 292 944 describes the preparation'); and the very next sentence withdraws it ('However, it is known that electronegative substituents ... distinctly hinder the reaction'), so it functions as the premise of an argument rather than as prior art the patent is distinguishing its process from. The cost of that ruling is recorded so a reviewer can overturn it: the A1 class term 'bromomethyl aromatics' comes only from that sentence and therefore appears in no A2 record, and 'methyl aromatics' appears here only because the WO 99/06339 sentence uses it as well. An extractor that emits a fourth record for the Houben-Weyl sentence is making a defensible reading, not an obvious error. The A1 term '3-bromomethylbenzoic acid' likewise appears in no record here, and that one needs no argument: its sentence says only that derivatives of it are valuable reactants in herbicide synthesis, which states no transformation at all.
